text:
The defending champions went to Finland and came home with two wins over Seattle and a four-game streak in which they outscored teams 23-7. At 16-3-2 the Hurricanes have the look of a team that never had a Stanley Cup hangover, and the trip doubled as a homecoming for Sebastian Aho and Jesperi Kotkaniemi.

This isn't a hot start built on bounces. Carolina has taken 61% of the expected goals (the quality of its chances) and 59% at 5v5, and our playoff odds have it in at 100%, with an 83% chance at the Metropolitan title and a projection near 119 points. Nikolaj Ehlers, Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake have been the best line: 12 goals for, one against. The Aho line with Andrei Svechnikov and William Carrier holds 67% of the chances.

What's worrying is mostly small print. Carolina has allowed about seven fewer goals than its chances against deserved, and Pyotr Kochetkov (4.5 goals saved above expected over his last five starts) is part of why. Goaltending can cool. The team also takes 3.57 penalties a game.

What to watch: as NHL.com's Tom Gulitti noted, Saturday was the first time all season Carolina had its full lineup, with Jordan Staal, last spring's Conn Smythe winner, back from a calf injury. Mark Jankowski is running hot, too (six points in his last ten). A full roster on a team this good is the scary part.
